riddles.question: What starts with T, ends with T, and has T in it?
hints: Think about the literal spelling of the riddle.
It is a household item used for serving a warm beverage.
It starts and ends with the letter 'T' and contains 'T' (tea-pot).

riddles.question: What kind of ship had two mates but no captain?
hints: It's not an actual vessel that floats on water.
It describes a personal connection between romantic partners.
The word ends in '-ship' and involves companionship.

riddles.question: What loses its head in the morning but gets it back at night?
hints: You interact with it right before falling asleep.
It rests underneath your head when you lie down in bed.
When you get up, your head is no longer resting on it.

riddles.question: Paul’s height is six feet, he’s an assistant at a butcher’s shop, and wears size 9 shoes. What does he weigh?
hints: Pay close attention to where he works.
He doesn't weigh himself on a bathroom scale.
His job requires him to measure out cuts of food.

riddles.question: I sometimes run, but I can’t walk. What am I?
hints: It is a prominent feature on the center of your face.
It helps you smell and breathe.
When you have a cold, it tends to run.

riddles.question: I have cities but no houses, rivers but no water, and forests but no trees.
hints: It is a flat representation of geographic regions.
Travelers use it to navigate when planning a road trip.
It represents the world on a piece of paper.

riddles.question: What never speaks but always replies?
hints: You usually hear it bouncing off canyon walls or empty rooms.
It repeats the exact sound or words you shout out.
It has no voice of its own.

riddles.question: I have many teeth, but I never bite.
hints: You keep it in your bathroom drawer or vanity.
You use it while styling your hair in front of a mirror.
Its rows of fine plastic or metal prongs look like teeth.

riddles.question: If there are three apples and you take away two, how many do you have?
hints: Read the phrasing of the question very carefully.
Focus on who is doing the taking.
If you physically take two apples into your hands, that's how many you hold.

riddles.question: I am lighter than a feather, but nobody can hold me for very long. What am I?
hints: It is something you take continuously to stay alive.
You pull it into your lungs and let it back out.
Try holding it for five minutes and see how long you last.

riddles.question: What thrives when you feed it, but dies when you water it?
hints: It produces bright flames and intense heat in a fireplace.
You feed it logs or wood to keep it going.
Pouring liquid on it will put it out immediately.

riddles.question: What kind of room has no walls, doors or windows?
hints: It is a trick question playing on a specific English suffix.
It grows in damp, shady areas outdoors or in forests.
It is a type of fungus you might slice up on a pizza.

riddles.question: What runs all around a backyard, yet never moves?
hints: It outlines the property perimeter of a suburban home.
It keeps pets or children safely contained in a yard.
It stays permanently fixed in place while outlining the yard.
